subject: mathematics
question_text: Find p if the vectors a + b + c, a + pb + 2c and −a + b + c are coplanar, where a, b, c are non-coplanar.

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.73, chapter 7 PRODUCT OF VECTORS, Short Answer question 28. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The split gives half the marks to the determinant of coefficients and a full mark to saying why [a b c] may be divided out, which is the step that makes the whole method legal. Both evaluations agree at 2p − 4: the first-row expansion gives (p − 2) − (1 + 2) + (1 + p), and the first-column expansion gives (p − 2) − 0 − (2 − p). Substituting p = 2 gives 1(0) − 1(3) + 1(3) = 0 exactly. A second, independent check: with p = 2 the middle vector a + 2b + 2c equals (3u + w)/2, where u = a + b + c and w = −a + b + c, so it genuinely lies in the plane of the other two. Paper position: Maths-1A Section B prints eight short answers of which the student writes any six, each worth 4 marks, under the 2026-27 pattern; Product of Vectors supplies one of them. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find p — how the three vectors become rows of numbers, and what you do with the determinant.

steps.label: Write the coefficients as rows
steps.margin_note: First mark. [a b c] ≠ 0 is what allows it to be cancelled; say so before dividing by it.
steps.memory_tip: Read off the coefficients of a, b, c as one row per vector. The basis box product factors out.

steps.why: Writing each vector by its coefficients on a, b, c turns the box product into a number times [a b c], and that number is the determinant of the coefficients.
common_mistakes: Treating a, b, c as i, j, k and losing the factor [a b c].
Setting [u v w] = 0 without saying why [a b c] may be divided out.

steps.label: Expand the determinant
steps.margin_note: Half the marks. The rows are the coefficients in the order a, b, c, including the −1 in the third row.
steps.memory_tip: One row per vector: (1, 1, 1), (1, p, 2), (−1, 1, 1). The minus sign is part of the row.

recall.must_convey: That the coefficient determinant expands to 2p − 4.

steps.why: Expanding along a different line must give the same expression in p; the two agree, so the cofactor signs were handled correctly.
common_mistakes: Reading the third row as (1, 1, 1) and losing the minus on a.

steps.label: Solve for p and check
steps.margin_note: Last mark. With p = 2 the middle vector is (3u + w)/2, so it really does lie in the plane of u and w.
steps.memory_tip: 2p = 4 gives p = 2. Put it back: the determinant must read exactly 0.
